analysis.title: US Economic Weekly: Sep jobs preview: Don't fall for the headline
key_insights: BofA forecasts Sep nonfarm payrolls at +60k (private +50k), below the 100k consensus, down from 162k in Aug. The weakness is attributed mainly to payback from Aug's unusually favorable seasonal factors.

Underlying job growth is estimated at 100k+ based on benign claims, improving ADP readings and other labor indicators. Initial and continuing claims are at historic lows, including during the survey week.
Unemployment rate forecast to stay at 4.1% for a third month with participation steady at 61.6%. There is a risk of 4.2% because household employment rose 569k in Aug and could pay back.

Aug seasonal adjustment was close to zero versus a 178k subtraction in Aug '25. BofA ties this partly to a four-week survey interval in Aug '26 versus five weeks in '24 and '25, which raises the risk of Sep payback.

Sector view: construction should post a seventh straight gain on data-center investment, manufacturing is firm, and professional & business services has added jobs for eight straight months. Leisure & hospitality and local government education should soften after driving much of Aug's upside.

TPS work-authorization suspension for Haitian nationals (July 27) has not yet shown in payrolls. About 200k Haitian TPS holders were in the workforce. BofA's base case is a gradual, mild headwind to payrolls and participation with little effect on the u-rate, but there is downside risk in Sep.
Breakeven job growth is estimated at 20k/month and may be modestly higher given tighter immigration. Even the below-consensus forecast keeps the 3-month average (80k) well above breakeven.

Markets price close to 100bp of hikes over the next year and nearly a 75% chance of an October hike. Fed Chair Warsh stressed benign claims and a stable u-rate over weak job growth. BofA thinks Sep CPI matters more than the jobs report for October.

Aug PCE (released with annual revisions on 9/30) is forecast at +0.4% m/m headline and +0.3% m/m core. Methodological changes are expected to cut y/y headline and core by about 0.2pp, to 3.6% headline and 3.2% core y/y.

Federal net interest expense hit a record 3.3% of GDP in 2Q 2026, above the 3.2% peak in 1991 when the 10y yield was around 7%. BofA argues yields may need to rise much further before Washington turns to fiscal discipline.
Household assets rose above 10x liabilities for the first time in six decades after the 2Q equity surge. A 20% equity drop would only take the ratio to 9.5, still above levels before 2H 2025.
3Q GDP tracking is unchanged at 3.0% q/q saar and 2Q tracking is 1.8%. BofA's official 3Q forecast is 2.4%. ISM manufacturing for Sep is tracked at 55.0 versus 54.6 in Aug.

BofA keeps its out-of-consensus call that the Fed hikes 25bp in both Oct and Dec 2026, taking the funds rate midpoint to 4.375%. The Fed hiked 25bp at the Sep meeting with a hawkish message, and the statement dropped language linking inflation to supply shocks.

BofA cut 4Q/4Q 2026 growth by 20bp to 2.1% on higher oil and shrinking prospects of a deal to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz. It still forecasts 4Q/4Q core PCE at 3.3% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027, with headline raised on energy and food prices from the Iran war.
Recent Fed speakers lean hawkish. Paulson, Williams, Barr, Hammack, Musalem and Schmid have signaled further tightening may be needed, and Williams said another hike by year-end may be appropriate.
BofA card data shows total card spending per household up 6.9% y/y in the week ending Sep 19, with gas spending up 26.5% y/y. Total card spending excluding gas was up 5.7%.

risk_factors: Larger-than-expected seasonal payback in Sep payrolls.
TPS visa revocations hitting Sep payrolls and participation more than the gradual path BofA assumes.
Household employment payback could lift the u-rate to 4.2%.
Upside inflation risks from AI-related investment, labor supply constraints, trade policy, the Iran war and weather-related supply shocks.
Rising oil prices raising energy inflation and reducing real consumer spending and capex.
Long-end yields rising further, with fiscal discipline unlikely until yields rise significantly.

vol_and_positioning: Markets price close to 100bp of Fed rate increases over the next year, with nearly a 75% likelihood of an October hike at the time of writing.

geopolitical: Strait of Hormuz: BofA sees shrinking prospects of a deal to fully reopen it, which adds energy-related inflation.

Tighter immigration policy continues to restrain labor supply.

tension_points.bull_case: Underlying job growth is resilient at 100k+, with claims at historic lows, rising ADP and broadening hiring across construction, manufacturing and professional services.
tension_points.bear_case: The 60k headline could undershoot further if seasonal payback is larger, TPS revocations hit all at once, or the u-rate rises to 4.2% on household employment payback.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Sep payroll print well below 60k with a u-rate above 4.2% would challenge the view that weakness is only seasonal payback.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA expects the Fed to hike 25bp in Oct and Dec given solid growth, a balanced labor market and inflation too high.
tension_points.bear_case: Jobs data could shift pricing if weak, though BofA says the jobs report should not be decisive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A soft Sep CPI would weaken the case for an October hike, since BofA says CPI matters more than jobs.
